decision.trend: Research has been focused on understanding the phase evolution and microstructure refinement of high-entropy alloys (HEAs) through various processing techniques such as mechanical alloying, spark plasma sintering, and aging treatments. The studies have shown that these techniques can significantly influence the mechanical properties and phase transformations of HEAs. For instance, mechanical alloying and spark plasma sintering can lead to the formation of nanocrystalline solid solution microstructures, while aging treatments can induce phase transformations and changes in mechanical properties.
decision.unsolved: Despite the progress made in understanding the processing-structure-property relationships of HEAs, there is still a lack of understanding on how to control the phase evolution and microstructure refinement to achieve desired mechanical properties. Specifically, the development of a method to control the phase evolution in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEAs remains an open question.
decision.why: The next step would be to develop a machine learning-based approach to model and predict the phase transformations in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEAs under various processing conditions. This would enable the identification of optimal processing parameters to achieve desired phase evolution and mechanical properties. The use of machine learning algorithms can help to uncover complex relationships between processing conditions, phase transformations, and mechanical properties, and provide a predictive tool for the design of new HEAs with tailored properties.
